reaction.episode: CORRECTION through 2026-11-04: SPX 7,688.62, 1.99% below its 120-day high of 7,844.52, sitting on its 50-day at 7,692.97 (-0.06%) and 5.03% above its 200-day at 7,320.35. SMH is in Zone 2 at 504.27 (-24.94% from its high, 3.25% below its 200-day) and NVDA in Zone 1 at 200.13. VIX fell to 16.61 after a 21.15 five-day high, HY OAS is 3.4% and calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: A held SPX close above 7,820 (top of the failure zone) with SMH reclaiming its 50-day at 569.98 voids the correction stance; a HY OAS close above 4% voids the rotation read and the ladder with it.

ladder.response: Re-check Tranche A conditions (Zone 2 print already in hand plus capitulation tally at 3 of 6 or better); prepare the AVGO/DDOG tier-A list, do not chase the breakdown.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below the 470 Zone 2 floor

ladder.response: Treat as a sell/short-covering rally, not a bottom; no new adds on the first bounce, wait for the failure-zone retest verdict.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into the 7,750-7,820 failure zone or SMH into 580-600

ladder.response: Stand down: the rotation read is void, the ladder is void, move to capital preservation until credit re-calms.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4% or VIX closes above 25

ladder.response: Probe the Zone 2 names — AVGO and DDOG first — at pre-sized probe scale, not full Tranche A.
ladder.trigger: SMH holds a second low above 470 with VIX rolling over from 21.15 and the tally at 3 of 4 or better

reaction.trapRisk: Today's bounce is the trap case in miniature: SPX rose 1.58% and QQQ 1.22% while SMH fell 2.75% and NVDA fell 3.17% — the bounce is broad-market, not in the complex that has to bottom. Chasing the first bounce into 7,750-7,820 risks a pivot-and-fail; entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict, not the first green day.

strategyPosture: Watch. SMH sits inside Zone 2 and NVDA in Zone 1 with tier-A conviction names 34-50% below their highs on still-growing revenue, but the capitulation tally is only 2 of 4, the volume-climax and VIX-rollover signals are unconfirmed, and the day's bounce skipped semis entirely. Hold bills, keep Tranche A prepared, add nothing on a one-day bounce.

themes.counterRead: Rotation is the right label today, but the divergence itself is the risk: the same handful of names that carried the index are the ones falling, so if credit flips — HY OAS toward 4% — the rotation story becomes a rollover story fast. The gap is real and worth tracking, not dismissing.
themes.dataAnchor: The calm is index-level only: Mag7 names average 14.07% below their 52-week highs against SPY at 1.9%, a 12.17-point divergence gap, with GOOGL the weakest at 29.3% below its high and MSFT the strongest at 0.6%. Credit confirms the rotation read rather than a rollover: bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% (far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.4% and calm.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The broad tape looks calm — SPX rose 1.58% to 7,688.62 and sits just 1.99% below its 120-day high — so the market reads the selloff as contained.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4% or the Mag7-SPY divergence gap widening past 15 points while SPX breaks its 50-day at 7,692.97.

themes.counterRead: The story had run past the data — policy risk in merchant power was unpriced, and the election exposed it. The washout may still overshoot: VST insiders bought $1.17M at the trough and the name trades at 2.3x sales, so the dislocation is now two-sided and needs a policy read, not a momentum read.
themes.dataAnchor: The Nov 3 midterm sweep repriced that story in one session: VST fell 13.25% on the day (down 24.55% over the month, 39.9% below its 52-week high, RSI 31.6), GEV fell 8.96%, PWR fell 10.8%, ETN fell 8.98%, and CEG sank 8% on headlines tying the drop directly to the election outcome. VST's revenue is still growing 19.1% YoY, but its revenue inflection is DETERIORATING and its 1-month trend is -26.3%.
themes.label: AI Power Trade Repriced by the Election
themes.narrative: Merchant power generators were priced as certain AI beneficiaries — the story ran that hyperscaler power demand made VST, CEG and the nuclear complex a one-way trade.
themes.watchFor: A second day of merchant-power selling after the election headlines fade, or VST reclaiming its 50-day with insider buying continuing.

themes.counterRead: The bounce skipped the complex entirely — SPX rose 1.58% and QQQ 1.22% while SMH fell 2.75% and NVDA fell 3.17% — so there is no bottoming signal yet, only zone occupancy. Price and fundamentals are moving in opposite directions, which is the setup, not the entry: the mechanical tally is only 2 of 4, with volume-climax reversal and VIX rollover both unconfirmed.
themes.dataAnchor: SMH closed at 504.27 inside Zone 2 (470-505) and NVDA at 200.13 inside Zone 1 (200-210), with NVDA down 17.77% from its high and 9.53% below its 50-day. The fundamentals run the other way: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% YoY, AVGO 55% (score 80, conviction promotion at $326.18, 34.1% below its peak), LRCX 131.3% while 49.7% below its high. AVGO's gross margin is 67.8% with a 42.1% FCF margin.
themes.label: Semiconductors Inside the Buy Zone
themes.narrative: Semis are broken — SMH is down 24.94% from its high and 19.32% over 20 days, and the tape treats the complex as uninvestable.
themes.watchFor: SMH holding a second low above the 470 Zone 2 floor with volume climax and VIX rolling over from its 21.15 five-day high.

themes.counterRead: Growth has not broken — the multiple has. That is a DATA_AHEAD setup, but a cheap multiple is not a catalyst: DDOG's window is earnings August 2026 and the names need either a demand print or a broad risk turn before the gap closes. Screen, verify thesis, size nothing on the dislocation alone.
themes.dataAnchor: DDOG is 37.6% below its 52-week high with revenue growing 27.7% YoY, an 80% gross margin and a 29.2% FCF margin (top conviction, score 84, RSI 28.5). SNOW is 25% below its high on 34.3% revenue growth, NET 28.6% below on 34.7% growth, NOW 39.3% below with RSI 30.5. The dislocation list is broad and sentiment-driven, with RSI readings of 28-36 across DDOG, LRCX, TER and RDDT.
themes.label: Software and SaaS Washout
themes.narrative: Enterprise software is a value trap in a rates-higher world — the market reads the SaaS drawdown as a growth story ending.
themes.watchFor: DDOG or SNOW holding above their current lows on rising volume, or a revenue print that re-rates the group.

themes.counterRead: Rates and equities agree that this is a valuation drawdown, not a funding crack — the bond market is not confirming the equity fear. The risk is the other direction: if the December FOMC delivers a hawkish surprise, the VIX collapse reverses and the 5.5% 10-year trigger comes back into play.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year sits at 4.95% with the 2-year at 4.61% and the curve at +0.34, the real 10-year at 2.69%, and the policy rate at 3.88%. Yet VIX collapsed 20.26% in a day to 16.61 after a five-day high of 21.15, HY OAS is 3.4% and calm, and IWM rose 1.62% on the day with a 1.06% one-month gain — small caps are not pricing a credit event.
themes.label: Credit Calm, Rates Higher, VIX Collapsing
themes.narrative: The Fed signals higher rates into the Dec 8-9 FOMC, so the market reads rates as the binding constraint and expects the tape to stay heavy.
themes.watchFor: VIX closing back above 21.15 or the 10-year closing above 5.2% into the Dec 8-9 FOMC.

watchFor: SMH daily close vs the 470 Zone 2 floor and vs its 200-day at 521.22
NVDA close vs the 200 Zone 1 floor and the 175-185 Zone 2 band
VIX close vs its 21.15 five-day high for rollover confirmation and vs 25 for stand-down
HY OAS vs the 4% stand-down line
SPX close vs the 7,750-7,820 failure zone
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in semis: either SMH breaks the 470 Zone 2 floor and the washout completes, or the failure-zone retest at SPX 7,750-7,820 and SMH 580-600 decides whether this bounce is a bottom or a bull trap. The trigger is SMH's second-low behavior plus VIX rollover confirmation.
